name: ANSI three-input AND gate
summary: D-shaped AND outline with three input leads; the output is high only when all three inputs are high.
description: The three-input AND keeps the familiar flat-backed D outline and simply adds a third input lead on the flat side. All three inputs must be at logic 1 in positive logic for the output to be at logic 1. Packages such as triple three-input AND devices provide this function directly.

Drafters use the wider gate rather than cascading two-input gates when the function is a single permissive with three conditions, such as guard closed, pressure healthy and mode selected. A single symbol keeps the logic readable and avoids implying an intermediate signal that does not exist.
The outline does not show whether an unused input is tied high when a three-input part is used for two signals. Unused inputs on the physical device need a defined level shown on the schematic.
readingNotes: Count the input leads; a third input is easy to overlook where leads are closely spaced.
Check unused inputs are tied to a defined level.
drawingChecklist: Space the three inputs evenly along the flat side.
Show tie-offs for unused inputs on multi-input packages.
distinction: A two-input AND followed by another AND produces the same logic but implies an intermediate net.
